question: Should Gateway allow scheme-level browser-origin wildcards such as `chrome-extension://*`, and should that grammar live inside `allowedOrigins` or a constrained pattern field?
rationale: The source failure is clear, but this changes browser-origin authorization semantics for Gateway clients and current related PRs do not establish the permanent wildcard grammar or security posture.

options.title: Define constrained pattern contract
options.body: Add a reviewed, narrow pattern grammar with tests, docs, and audit handling instead of accepting arbitrary trailing-prefix wildcards.

options.title: Keep exact origins only
options.body: Continue with exact opaque-origin fixes and reject changing-extension-ID wildcards as outside the current Gateway origin policy.

options.title: Allow Chrome extension wildcard only
options.body: Permit `chrome-extension://*` in the existing allowlist with scheme-specific matching and negative security tests.

recommendation.title: Define constrained pattern contract
recommendation.body: Add a reviewed, narrow pattern grammar with tests, docs, and audit handling instead of accepting arbitrary trailing-prefix wildcards.

likelyOwner.reason: He introduced the current Gateway browser-origin hardening and is the strongest history-backed owner for the security-boundary decision.
